# MDL104 · `missing-final-newline`

<!-- Generated by tools/gendocs from internal/rules: do not edit. -->

The file does not end with a newline.

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | loading |
| Default severity | error |
| Fix | safe |
| Flags | unsuppressible |
| Design references | §3.2, cases 02, 18 |

## Why

mydumper's pre-processor only appends `= 1` to a line when it meets the `\n` that ends it. A flag such as `routines` on the last line of a file without a final newline stays `routines`, which GLib rejects, so mydumper ignores the whole file.

Even when the last line is a key/value pair, a missing final newline is a latent risk: anything a script appends to the file is glued to that line.

## Example

❌ Before:

```text
[mydumper]
routines
```

(`\r`, `\t` and `\xHH` stand for the bytes they name, `·` for a trailing space)

```text
2:9-2:9 error MDL104[missing-final-newline] the last line has no newline, so mydumper's pre-processor does not append `= 1` to `routines` (GLib: Key file contains line “routines” which is not a key-value pair, group, or comment)
  = mydumper ignores this entire file: it only logs a WARNING ("Failed to load config file") and runs with its defaults, exit code 0.
  fix (safe): Add a final newline
```

✅ After `mydumper-lint check --fix`:

```ini
[mydumper]
routines
```

## Configuration

Enabled by default. To change its severity or turn it off:

```yaml
rules:
  severity:
    MDL104: warning   # or error, info, off
```

Its diagnostics mean mydumper ignores the whole file: they cannot be suppressed by comments, only by the configuration or `--ignore`.
